## Inscription / 题献
===Original===

To Dr. Burney
Oh, Author of my being!﻿—far more dear

To me than light, than nourishment, or rest,

Hygeia’s blessings, Rapture’s burning tear,

Or the lifeblood that mantles in my breast!
If in my heart the love of Virtue glows,

’Twas planted there by an unerring rule;

From thy example the pure flame arose,

Thy life, my precept﻿—thy good works, my school.
Could my weak pow’rs thy num’rous virtues trace,

By filial love each fear should be repress’d,

The blush of Incapacity I’d chase,

And stand, Recorder of thy worth, confess’d:
But since my niggard stars that gift refuse,

Concealment is the only boon I claim;

Obscure be still the unsuccessful Muse,

Who cannot raise, but would not sink, thy fame.
Oh! of my life at once the source and joy!

If e’er thy eyes these feeble lines survey,

Let not their folly their intent destroy;

Accept the tribute﻿—but forget the lay.

===Chinese===

献给伯尼博士
哦，我生命的创造者！——你于我
比光明更亲，比滋养、比安眠更亲，
比许癸厄亚的福佑、比狂喜滚烫的热泪更亲，
比涌上我胸头的生命之血更亲！
倘我心头有爱德之火在烧，
那是一只从不误引的手所栽；
这纯焰自你的榜样中升起，
你的一生是我的训诫——你的善行是我的学堂。
倘若我微弱之力描得下你万千美德，
儿女之爱自会压住每一分惶恐，
我必逐去这无力之愧，
坦然立作你德行的记录者：
无奈吝啬的星辰不肯赐这禀赋，
我只求一桩恩典：将我隐去；
让这不成的缪斯依旧默默无闻——
她抬不高你的名声，却也不肯让它沉。
哦！你是我生命之源，又是我生命之乐！
倘你的眼睛偶尔扫过这些孱弱的诗行，
别让它们的愚拙毁了它们的心意；
请收下这份敬献——然后忘掉这首诗。

## Dedication To the Authors of the *Monthly* and *Critical* Reviews / 献辞——致《每月评论》与《批评评论》的作者们
===Original===

Gentlemen,
The liberty which I take in addressing to you the trifling production of a few idle hours, will doubtless move your wonder, and probably your contempt. I will not, however, with the futility of apologies, intrude upon your time, but briefly acknowledge the motives of my temerity; lest, by a premature exercise of that patience which I hope will befriend me, I should lessen its benevolence, and be accessary to my own condemnation.
Without name, without recommendation, and unknown alike to success and disgrace, to whom can I so properly apply for patronage, as to those who publicly profess themselves inspectors of all literary performances?
The extensive plan of your critical observations﻿—which, not confined to works of utility or ingenuity, is equally open to those of frivolous amusement﻿—and, yet worse than frivolous, dullness﻿—encourages me to seek for your protection, since﻿—perhaps for my sins!﻿—it entitles me to your annotations. To resent, therefore, this offering, however insignificant, would ill become the universality of your undertaking; though not to despise it may, alas! be out of your power.
The language of adulation, and the incense of flattery, though the natural inheritance, and constant resource, from time immemorial, of the dedicator, to me offer nothing but the wistful regret that I dare not invoke their aid. Sinister views would be imputed to all I could say; since, thus situated, to extol your judgment, would seem the effect of art, and to celebrate your impartiality, be attributing to suspecting it.
As magistrates of the press, and censors for the public﻿—to which you are bound by the sacred ties of integrity to exert the most spirited impartiality, and to which your suffrages should carry the marks of pure, dauntless, irrefragable truth﻿—to appeal to your *mercy*, were to solicit your dishonour; and therefore﻿—though ’tis sweeter than frankincense﻿—more grateful to the senses than all the odorous perfumes of Arabia﻿—and though

> It droppeth like the gentle rain from heaven

Upon the place beneath﻿—

I court it not! to your justice alone I am intitled, and by that I must abide. Your engagements are not to the supplicating authors; but to the candid public, which will not fail to crave

> The penalty and forfeit of your bond.

===Chinese===

诸位先生：
我贸然把几段闲散时辰的区区产物寄奉诸位，这份唐突，想必会引起诸位的惊异，多半还有轻蔑。但我不用无用的道歉去侵占诸位的时间，只简短招认我胆大包天的动机；免得过早动用我希望会施惠于我的那份耐心，反而折损了它的仁厚，亲手给自己的定罪添上一笔。
无姓名，无荐引，于成功与丢脸同属无名之辈——赞助之请，我还能递给谁，比递给诸位更妥当呢？诸位可是公开自任一切文字作品的检查官的。
诸位批评宏图之广——不限于有用或有才气的著作，对仅供无聊消遣的、乃至比无聊更糟的沉闷之作，也一体开放——这鼓励我来寻求诸位的庇护；因为——多半是我造了孽！——这使我够格领受诸位的批注。因此，无论这份献物多么微不足道，为它动怒都有失诸位事业的包罗万象；虽然不鄙夷它，唉！恐怕非诸位之力所能及。
谄媚的辞令与奉承的香火，虽自太古以来便是题献者的天然遗产与惯常资粮，于我却只留下一腔怅惘：我不敢请它们帮忙。我说的每一句，都会被安上别有用心的罪名；因为处在我这境地，盛赞诸位的鉴裁，倒像是手腕作祟；歌颂诸位的公正，反倒坐实了对它的疑心。
作为出版界的执政官、公众的监察官——诸位受廉洁的神圣约束，必须拿出最刚健的不偏不倚，诸位的裁断也应盖上纯粹、无畏、无可辩驳的真理之印——向诸位的慈悲呼吁，无异于恳求诸位自毁清誉；因此——尽管它比乳香更甜，比阿拉伯一切芬芳的香膏更熨帖感官，尽管

> 它像从天上轻轻降下的细雨，
> 落在下界的土地上——

我不乞求它！我名下应得的只有诸位的公正，我也必须服从它。诸位所承担的对象，不是哀求的作者，而是坦率的公众；公众必定会来索取

> 那笔债券的罚金与抵押。

===Original===

No hackneyed writer, inured to abuse, and callous to criticism, here braves your severity;﻿—neither does a half-starved garreteer,

> Oblig’d by hunger﻿—and request of friends﻿—

implore your lenity: your examination will be alike unbiased by partiality and prejudice;﻿—no refractory murmuring will follow your censure, no private interest will be gratified by your praise.
Let not the anxious solicitude with which I recommend myself to your notice, expose me to your derision. Remember, Gentlemen, you were all young writers once, and the most experienced veteran of your corps may, by recollecting his first publication, renovate his first terrors, and learn to allow for mine. For though courage is one of the noblest virtues of this nether sphere; and though scarcely more requisite in the field of battle, to guard the fighting hero from disgrace, than in the private commerce of the world, to ward off that littleness of soul which leads, by steps imperceptible, to all the base train of the inferior passions, and by which the too timid mind is betrayed into a servility derogatory to the dignity of human nature! yet is it a virtue of no necessity in a situation such as mine; a situation which removes, even from cowardice itself, the sting of ignominy;﻿—for surely that courage may easily be dispensed with, which would rather excite disgust than admiration! Indeed, it is the peculiar privilege of an author, to rob terror of contempt, and pusillanimity of reproach.
*Here let me rest*﻿—and snatch myself, while I yet am able, from the fascination of *egotism*:﻿—a monster who has more votaries than ever did homage to the most popular deity of antiquity; and whose singular quality is, that while he excites a blind and involuntary adoration in almost every individual, his influence is universally disallowed, his power universally contemned, and his worship, even by his followers, never mentioned but with abhorence.
In addressing you jointly, I mean but to mark the generous sentiments by which liberal criticism, to the utter annihilation of envy, jealousy, and all selfish views, ought to be distinguished.
I have the honour to be,

**Gentlemen**,

Your most obedient

Humble Servant,

**—﻿—﻿— —﻿—﻿—**

===Chinese===

在此向诸位的严厉叫阵的，不是那类挨惯了骂、批评磨出了茧的老练写手；也不是那类半饿着肚子的阁楼客，

> 迫于饥饿——又拗不过朋友们的恳求——

来哀求诸位的高抬贵手：诸位评审起来，既不会被偏爱好污，也不会被成见左右；诸位贬斥之后，不会有梗着脖子的怨言跟随，诸位褒扬之下，也没有私利得偿。
我这样焦灼地把自己荐到诸位眼下，可别因此招来诸位的讪笑。请记住，诸位先生，你们从前也都是年轻作家；贵团最老练的老兵，只消回想一下自己的第一本书，初版时的那阵恐怖便会还魂，便学会体谅我的这一阵。虽说勇气是这下界最高贵的德行之一；虽说在战场上，保英雄之脸不为临阵脱逃所辱，所需于它的，几乎不多于在世俗的私人往来中，靠它挡开那种灵魂的渺小——那渺小以不觉察的步子，一路引向底下那串卑贱的情欲，叫过于怯懦的心滑进一种有损人类尊严的奴颜！可在我这样的处境里，它偏偏是一种不必要的德行；这处境连怯懦本身都免去了耻辱之刺；——因为那种只会招人厌恶、赚不来钦佩的勇气，省了也罢！的确，把恐怖身上的轻蔑剥掉、把怯懦身上的责骂剥掉，正是作者独有的一项特权。
*就此打住*——趁还来得及，把自己从*自我主义*的魅惑里一把拽出来：——那是一头怪物，香火之盛，超过古时任何一位走红的神祇；而它的独门品性是：它几乎在每个人心里激起一种盲目的、不由自主的崇拜，它的影响却无人肯认，它的权能无人不鄙，对它的礼拜，连它的信众自己提起来也无不憎嫌。
联名奉致二位，无非想标出那副慷慨的心肠——开明的批评，理应以它区别于他物，把嫉妒、猜忌与一切自私的盘算，斩尽杀绝。
我荣为

**诸位先生**

最恭顺的

卑贱仆人

**———— ——**

## Preface / 序
===Original===

In the republic of letters, there is no member of such inferior rank, or who is so much disdained by his brethren of the quill, as the humble novelist; nor is his fate less hard in the world at large, since, among the whole class of writers, perhaps not one can be named of which the votaries are more numerous but less respectable.
Yet, while in the annals of those few of our predecessors, to whom this species of writing is indebted for being saved from contempt, and rescued from depravity, we can trace such names as Rousseau, Johnson,1 Marivaux, Fielding, Richardson, and Smollett, no man need blush at starting from the same post, though many, nay, most men, may sigh at finding themselves distanced.
The following letters are presented to the public﻿—for such, by novel writers, novel readers will be called﻿—with a very singular mixture of timidity and confidence, resulting from the peculiar situation of the editor; who, though trembling for their success from a consciousness of their imperfections, yet fears not being involved in their disgrace, while happily wrapped up in a mantle of impenetrable obscurity.
To draw characters from nature, though not from life, and to mark the manners of the times, is the attempted plan of the following letters. For this purpose, a young female, educated in the most secluded retirement, makes, at the age of seventeen, her first appearance upon the great and busy stage of life; with a virtuous mind, a cultivated understanding, and a feeling heart, her ignorance of the forms, and inexperience in the manners of the world, occasion all the little incidents which these volumes record, and which form the natural progression of the life of a young woman of obscure birth, but conspicuous beauty, for the first six months after her *entrance into the world*.

===Chinese===

在文人共和国里，再没有哪个成员的地位这样低下，再没有谁这样遭同行笔杆子们的白眼，像这卑贱的小说家；他在大千世界里的命运也不见得好些：在整个作家阶层里，也许举不出第二种人，香火如此之旺，身份却如此之低。
不过，这一文体之所以免于轻蔑、免于堕落，全亏前代少数几位；在他们的名录里，我们数得出卢梭、约翰逊、1 马里沃、菲尔丁、理查逊和斯摩莱特这样的名字——既然如此，从同一条起跑线上出发，谁也不必脸红；尽管许多人，不，大多数人，会因被甩下而叹气。
以下书简奉呈于"公众"——小说家们就是这样称呼小说读者的——心情是怯懦与自信的一种十分奇特的混合物，这得归因于编者的特殊处境：一方面深知这些信的种种不足，为它们的成败战栗；另一方面又不怕同它们的耻辱搅在一起——因为他有幸襄在一件穿不透的无名之衣里。
从自然中——虽不是从真人身上——描画人物，并为时代的风尚留影，便是以下书简试图的方案。为此，一位在极幽闭的乡野中教养长大的少女，十七岁上，初次登上了人生这座又大又热闹的舞台；她心地纯正，见识有教养，心肠有感情；而她于世故形式的无知、于人情世故的无经历，便引出了这几卷书所记的全部小小事故——它们构成一个出身寒微、却美貌出众的年轻女子*进入社交界*头六个月里，自然而然的一段人生。

===Original===

Perhaps, were it possible to effect the total extirpation of novels, our young ladies in general, and boarding-school damsels in particular, might profit from their annihilation; but since the distemper they have spread seems incurable, since their contagion bids defiance to the medicine of advice or reprehension, and since they are found to baffle all the mental art of physic, save what is prescribed by the slow regimen of time, and bitter diet of experience; surely all attempts to contribute to the number of those which may be read, if not with advantage, at least without injury, ought rather to be encouraged than contemned.
Let me, therefore, prepare for disappointment those who, in the perusal of these sheets, entertain the gentle expectation of being transported to the fantastic regions of romance, where fiction is coloured by all the gay tints of luxurious imagination, where reason is an outcast, and where the sublimity of the *marvellous* rejects all aid from sober probability. The heroine of these memoirs, young, artless, and inexperienced, is

> No faultless Monster that the world ne’er saw;

===Chinese===

倘若能把小说连根拔尽，我们的一般小姐、尤其寄宿学校的女学生们，或许倒能从它们的绝迹中得些好处；可是它们散布的这场时疫看来无药可医，它们的传染对劝诫与责备这两味药公然不服，而且人们发现，它们能破掉医家的一切心药——只除了时间这服慢疗程、经验这剂苦口药；那么，凡是为了给"读来即使无益、至少无害"的小说添几本而作的努力，就理应受鼓励，而不该受鄙薄。
因此，请容我先给那些读者泼一瓢冷水——他们翻读这几页时，怀着一腔温柔的期待，盼着被载往传奇的幻境：在那儿，虚构被奢靡想象的一切艳色涂染；在那儿，理性是流放犯；在那儿，*奇观*的崇高拒绝一切清醒可能性的援助。这部记事的女主人公，年轻、质朴、不谙世事，她

> 不是那种世间从未见过的、完美无瑕的怪物；

===Original===

but the offspring of Nature, and of Nature in her simplest attire.
In all the arts, the value of copies can only be proportioned to the scarcity of originals: among sculptors and painters, a fine statue, or a beautiful picture, of some great master, may deservedly employ the imitative talents of young and inferior artists, that their appropriation to one spot may not wholly prevent the more general expansion of their excellence; but, among authors, the reverse is the case, since the noblest productions of literature are almost equally attainable with the meanest. In books, therefore, imitation cannot be shunned too sedulously; for the very perfection of a model which is frequently seen, serves but more forcibly to mark the inferiority of a copy.
To avoid what is common, without adopting what is unnatural, must limit the ambition of the vulgar herd of authors: however zealous, therefore, my veneration of the great writers I have mentioned, however I may feel myself enlightened by the knowledge of Johnson, charmed with the eloquence of Rousseau, softened by the pathetic powers of Richardson, and exhiliarated by the wit of Fielding and humour of Smollett, I yet presume not to attempt pursuing the same ground which they have tracked; whence, though they may have cleared the weeds, they have also culled the flowers; and, though they have rendered the path plain, they have left it barren.
The candour of my readers I have not the impertinence to doubt, and to their indulgence I am sensible I have no claim; I have, therefore, only to entreat, that my own words may not pronounce my condemnation; and that what I have here ventured to say in regard to imitation, may be understood as it is meant, in a general sense, and not be imputed to an opinion of my own originality, which I have not the vanity, the folly, or the blindness, to entertain.
Whatever may be the fate of these letters, the editor is satisfied they will meet with justice; and commits them to the press, though hopeless of fame, yet not regardless of censure.

===Chinese===

而是自然的孩子，而且是最素衣简裳的自然的孩子。
在一切艺术里，摹本的价值只能与原本的珍稀成正比：在雕塑家和画家里，某位大师的一尊好雕像或一幅好画，尽可以正当地占用年轻次要艺术家的摹仿才能，免得它们被独占一隅，其妙处便完全无从普遍流布；可在作家这里，情形恰恰相反，因为文学最高贵的出品，同最低贱的出品几乎同样唾手可得。所以对书籍，摹仿怎么小心躲避都不为过；因为一个时时被人见到的范本，它的完美恰恰更狠地照出摹本的低劣。
避开凡俗，又不取乖谬，这必定限制住芸芸众作家的雄心：因此，无论我对前面提到的那些大作家怎样敬仰，无论我如何自觉被约翰逊的学识照亮、被卢梭的雄辩迷住、被理查逊的悲悯软化、被菲尔丁的机智和斯摩莱特的谐趣提神，我都不敢妄想去重走他们踩过的地皮；他们固然清除了杂草，却也摘走了花；固然把路踏平了，却也把地留荒了。
读者诸君的公道，我不敢无礼地怀疑；他们的宽容，我自知无福消受；因此我只有一件事恳求：别让我自己的话宣判我自己的罪；我在此斗胆就摹仿所说的一番话，请照它的本意、按一般意义来理解，别算到"自以为独出机杼"的账上——这份心思，我没有那份虚荣、那份愚蠢或那份盲目去领受。
无论这些书简命运如何，编者确信它们会得到公正；于是把它们交付刊印——虽不指望名声，却也并非不在意责难。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

I Lady Howard to the Rev. Mr. Villars
Howard Grove, Kent.
Can anything, my good Sir, be more painful to a friendly mind, than a necessity of communicating disagreeable intelligence? Indeed it is sometimes difficult to determine, whether the relator or the receiver of evil tidings is most to be pitied.
I have just had a letter from Madame Duval; she is totally at a loss in what manner to behave; she seems desirous to repair the wrongs she has done, yet wishes the world to believe her blameless. She would fain cast upon another the odium of those misfortunes for which she alone is answerable. Her letter is violent, sometimes abusive, and that of *you!﻿—you*, to whom she is under obligations which are greater even than her faults, but to whose advice she wickedly imputes all the sufferings of her much injured daughter, the late Lady Belmont. The chief purport of her writing I will acquaint you with; the letter itself is not worthy your notice.
She tells me that she has, for many years past, been in continual expectation of making a journey to England, which prevented her writing for information concerning this melancholy subject, by giving her hopes of making personal enquiries; but family occurrences have still detained her in France, which country she now sees no prospect of quitting. She has, therefore, lately used her utmost endeavours to obtain a faithful account of whatever related to her *ill-advised* daughter; the result of which giving her *some reason* to apprehend, that, upon her deathbed, she bequeathed an infant orphan to the world, she most graciously says, that if *you*, with whom *she understands* the child is placed, will procure authentic proofs of its relationship to her, you may sent it to Paris, where she will properly provide for it.
This woman is, undoubtedly, at length, self-convicted of her most unnatural behaviour; it is evident, from her writing, that she is still as vulgar and illiterate as when her first husband, Mr. Evelyn, had the weakness to marry her; nor does she at all apologize for addressing herself to me, though I was only once in her company.
Her letter has excited in my daughter Mirvan, a strong desire to be informed of the motives which induced Madame Duval to abandon the unfortunate Lady Belmont, at a time when a mother’s protection was peculiarly necessary for her peace and her reputation.

===Chinese===

第一封 霍华德夫人致尊敬的维拉尔斯（Villars）牧师先生
肯特郡，霍华德林苑。
亲爱的先生，还有什么比不得不传递坏消息，更叫一颗友爱的心难受的呢？说实在的，坏消息的报信人和收信人到底哪个更可怜，有时真难断定。
我刚收到杜瓦尔夫人（Madame Duval）一封信；她全然不知该拿自己怎么办才好；她像是想弥补自己造下的亏欠，却又盼着世人相信她清白无辜。那些不幸，责任本在她一人，她却巴不得把骂名转嫁旁人。她的信写得暴戾，有时竟出恶言——骂的还是*您！——您*，她欠您的恩情比她的过错还大，可她却恶毒地把她那惨遭伤害的女儿、已故的贝尔蒙特夫人的全部苦难，都归罪于您的劝导。她这封信的要旨，我且说与您；信本身不配劳您的眼。
她告诉我，多年来她一直指望动身来英格兰，指望能当面打听，也就懒得为这桩伤心事写信问讯了；可家事一桩接一桩，把她绊在法国，如今也看不出有离开那国的指望。于是她最近费尽力气，想弄到一份关于她那*失计的*女儿的可靠报告；查出的结果让她*多少有理由*推测：女儿临终时，给这世界留下了一个襁褓中的孤儿。于是她恩典浩荡地说：倘若*您*——*据她所闻*，孩子是放在您那儿的——能办出孩子与她血缘关系的正式凭据，您可以把孩子送到巴黎去，她自会妥当安顿。
这个女人，毫无疑问，到头来在自己笔下招认了自己那最悖逆人情的行为；从她的信看得出，她如今还是那么粗俗、那么目不识丁，同她第一任丈夫伊夫林先生一时软弱娶她时毫无二致；她径直给我写信，也一点不道声不是——我统共只同她见过一回。
她这封信惹得我女儿米尔文太太生了强烈的心思，想弄明白：当年杜瓦尔夫人究竟出于什么动机，抛下了那不幸的贝尔蒙特夫人——在那样一个时节，母亲的维护，于她的安宁、于她的名声，都格外要紧。

===Original===

Notwithstanding I was personally acquainted with all the parties concerned in that affair, the subject always appeared of too delicate a nature to be spoken of with the principals; I cannot, therefore, satisfy Mrs. Mirvan otherwise than by applying to you.
By saying that you *may* send the child, Madame Duval aims at *conferring*, where she most *owes* obligation. I pretend not to give you advice; you, to whose generous protection this helpless orphan is indebted for everything, are the best and only judge of what she ought to do; but I am much concerned at the trouble and uneasiness which this unworthy woman may occasion you.
My daughter and my grandchild join with me in desiring to be most kindly remembered to the amiable girl; and they bid me remind you, that the annual visit to Howard Grove, which we were formerly promised, has been discontinued for more than four years.
I am, dear Sir, with great regard,

Your most obedient friend and servant,
M. Howard.

===Chinese===

那桩事里的各当事人，我虽都亲自认识，这题目却始终显得过于微妙，不便同当事人开口；因此，要满足米尔文太太，我只有来请教您。
杜瓦尔夫人说什么您*可以*把孩子送去，她是想在她最*亏欠*的地方*施恩*。我不敢给您出主意；这个孤苦无依的孤儿，一切都有赖您慷慨的庇护，她该怎么办，您是最好也是唯一的裁判；只是这个不值当的女人恐怕要给您添烦恼、添不安，这叫我挂心。
我女儿和外孙女同我一起，向那位可爱的姑娘致以最亲切的问候；她们还让我提醒您：从前许诺过的每年一趟霍华德林苑之行，到如今已经断四年多了。
亲爱的先生，我怀着十二分的敬意，是您

最恭顺的朋友与仆人，
M. 霍华德。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

II Mr. Villars to Lady Howard
Berry Hill, Dorsetshire.
Your Ladyship did but too well foresee the perplexity and uneasiness of which Madame Duval’s letter has been productive. However, I ought rather to be thankful that I have so many years remained unmolested, than repine at my present embarrassment; since it proves, at least, that this wretched woman is at length awakened to remorse.
In regard to my answer, I must humbly request your Ladyship to write to this effect: “That I would not, upon any account, intentionally offend Madame Duval; but that I have weighty, nay unanswerable reasons for detaining her granddaughter at present in England; the principal of which is, that it was the earnest desire of one to whose will she owes implicit duty. Madame Duval may be assured, that she meets with the utmost attention and tenderness; that her education, however short of my wishes, almost exceeds my abilities; and I flatter myself, when the time arrives that she shall pay her duty to her grandmother, Madame Duval will find no reason to be dissatisfied with what has been done for her.”
Your Ladyship will not, I am sure, be surprised at this answer. Madame Duval is by no means a proper companion or guardian for a young woman: she is at once uneducated and unprincipled; ungentle in temper, and unamiable in her manners. I have long known that she has persuaded herself to harbour an aversion for me﻿—Unhappy woman! I can only regard her as an object of pity!
I dare not hesitate at a request from Mrs. Mirvan; yet, in complying with it, I shall, for her own sake, be as concise as I possibly can; since the cruel transactions which preceded the birth of my ward can afford no entertainment to a mind so humane as hers.
Your Ladyship may probably have heard, that I had the honour to accompany Mr. Evelyn, the grandfather of my young charge, when upon his travels, in the capacity of a tutor. His unhappy marriage, immediately upon his return to England, with Madame Duval, then a waiting-girl at a tavern, contrary to the advice and entreaties of all his friends, among whom I was myself the most urgent, induced him to abandon his native land, and fix his abode in France.

===Chinese===

第二封 维拉尔斯先生致霍华德夫人
多塞特郡，贝里山。
杜瓦尔夫人的信招来的这许多烦乱与不安，夫人您实在不幸言中。不过，我与其为眼下的尴尬怨叹，倒不如感恩：这么多年我竟得安然无事；何况这封信至少证明，这个可怜的女人终于悔意醒了。
至于我的回话，只好恳请夫人代笔，大意如此："我无论如何无意开罪杜瓦尔夫人；但有几个重大乃至无可辩驳的理由，使我暂留她的外孙女于英格兰；其中头一条是：这是一位她理应绝对服从其遗命的人的恳切心愿。杜瓦尔夫人尽管放心：孩子在这里受着最周到的照料与疼爱；她的教养虽不及我的期望，却几乎超出我的财力；我自信，等将来她去外婆跟前尽礼时，杜瓦尔夫人对她所受的照拂，找不出半点可以不满的地方。"
夫人想必不会对这个回答感到意外。杜瓦尔夫人断不是年轻女子的合适伴侣或监护人：她既无教养又无原则；性情不温和，举止不可亲。我早就知道，她说服了自己，心里存着对我的嫌恶——不幸的女人！我只能把她当作一个可怜的对象！
米尔文太太的请求，我不敢迟疑；只是照办时，为她着想，我要尽量从简：我这位被监护人出世之前那些残酷的经过，实在供不出什么可娱她那样一副仁心肠的东西。
夫人多半听说过，我这年轻被监护人的祖父伊夫林先生游历欧陆时，我有幸以导师的身份随行。他一回到英格兰，便不顾所有亲友的劝阻与恳求——其中数我劝得最急——不幸娶了杜瓦尔夫人，其时她是一家酒馆的侍女；这桩婚事逼得他离弃故土，定居法国。

===Original===

Thither he was followed by shame and repentance; feelings which his heart was not framed to support; for, notwithstanding he had been too weak to resist the allurements of beauty, which nature, though a niggard to her of every other boon, had with a lavish hand bestowed on his wife; yet he was a young man of excellent character, and, till thus unaccountably infatuated, of unblemished conduct. He survived this ill-judged marriage but two years. Upon his deathbed, with an unsteady hand, he wrote me the following note:

> “My friend, forget your resentment, in favour of your humanity;﻿—a father, trembling for the welfare of his child, bequeaths her to your care. O Villars! hear! pity! And relieve me!”

===Chinese===

耻辱与悔恨跟着他到了那边；而他的心天生承受不起这两种情感。虽说大自然对妻子别样悭吝，唯独把美貌慷慨地、成把地撒给了她，而他太软弱，抵制不了这诱惑；可他原本是个品行极好的青年，直到这场莫名其妙的痴迷之前，操行无瑕。这段失算的婚姻，他只熬过两年。临终的病榻上，他用一只发颤的手，给我写来这几行字：

> "我的朋友，请把你的怨恨化入你的仁心；——一个为孩子的福祉发抖的父亲，把她托付给你。哦，维拉尔斯！听着！怜悯！救救我！"

===Original===

Had my circumstances permitted me, I should have answered these words by an immediate journey to Paris; but I was obliged to act by the agency of a friend, who was upon the spot, and present at the opening of the will.
Mr. Evelyn left to me a legacy of a thousand pounds, and the sole guardianship of his daughter’s person till her eighteenth year; conjuring me, in the most affecting terms, to take the charge of her education till she was able to act with propriety for herself; but, in regard to fortune, he left her wholly dependent on her mother, to whose tenderness he earnestly recommended her.
Thus, though he would not, to a woman lowbred and illiberal as Mrs. Evelyn, trust the conduct and morals of his daughter, he nevertheless thought proper to secure to her the respect and duty to which, from her own child, were certainly her due; but unhappily, it never occurred to him that the mother, on her part, could fail in affection or justice.
Miss Evelyn, Madam, from the second to the eighteenth year of her life, was brought up under my care, and, except when at school under my roof. I need not speak to your Ladyship of the virtues of that excellent young creature. She loved me as her father; nor was Mrs. Villars less valued by her; while to me she became so dear, that her loss was little less afflicting than that which I have since sustained of Mrs. Villars herself.
At that period of her life we parted; her mother, then married to Monsieur Duval, sent for her to Paris. How often have I since regretted that I did not accompany her thither! Protected and supported by me, the misery and disgrace which awaited her might perhaps have been avoided. But, to be brief﻿—Madame Duval, at the instigation of her husband, earnestly, or rather tyrannically, endeavoured to effect a union between Miss Evelyn and one of his nephews. And, when she found her power inadequate to her attempt, enraged at her noncompliance, she treated her with the grossest unkindness, and threatened her with poverty and ruin.
Miss Evelyn, to whom wrath and violence had hitherto been strangers, soon grew weary of such usage; and rashly, and without a witness, consented to a private marriage with Sir John Belmont, a very profligate young man, who had but too successfully found means to insinuate himself into her favour. He promised to conduct her to England﻿—he did.﻿—O, Madam, you know the rest!

===Chinese===

倘若境况允许，我本该即刻亲赴巴黎，来回答这几句话；可我只好借一位朋友之手——他正在当地，也在启读遗嘱的现场。
伊夫林先生遗我一千镑，并把女儿十八岁以前的全部监护权交我一人；以最动情的字句恳求我担起她的教育，直到她能自己拿得体行事；至于财产，他把她完全托给了她母亲，恳切地把她荐于母亲的慈爱。
如此，他虽不肯把女儿的品行与操守托给伊夫林太太这样出身低微、心胸狭陋的女人，却仍觉得该保住她作为亲女之母理应得到的敬重与孝道；只是不幸，他从未想到，做母亲的，那一头也会亏了慈爱、亏了公道。
夫人，伊夫林小姐从两岁到十八岁，都在我膝下教养，除上学外，未曾离我家屋檐。那位好得罕见的年轻造物有怎样的美德，无须我向夫人絮叨。她爱我如父；维拉尔斯太太在她心里也不稍轻；而她于我竟那样亲，以至失去她之痛，比起我后来丧维拉尔斯太太之痛，相差无几。
她人生的那一站，我们分手了；她母亲——那时已改嫁杜瓦尔先生——召她去巴黎。此后我曾多少次悔恨，没陪她同去！有我护持，等着她的那场苦难与耻辱，或许原可避开。简而言之——杜瓦尔夫人受丈夫怂恿，一心——不，是横暴地——要促成伊夫林小姐同他一个侄儿的婚事。待她发现自己的权力不足以如愿，又恨姑娘不从，便百般苛待于她，拿贫穷和毁灭作恐吓。
伊夫林小姐，生平从未识得暴怒与强横这等事物，很快就受不住这样的对待；一时孟浪，无人在侧作证，私自应允了同约翰·贝尔蒙特爵士（Sir John Belmont）的婚事——一个极其放荡的年轻人，而他想方设法博她的欢心，博得太成功了。他答应带她回英格兰——他带了。——哦，夫人，下文您是知道的！

===Original===

﻿—Disappointed of the fortune he expected, by the inexorable rancour of the Duvals, he infamously burnt the certificate of their marriage, and denied that they had ever been united.
She flew to me for protection. With what mixed transports of joy and anguish did I again see her! By my advice, she endeavoured to procure proofs of her marriage﻿—but in vain; her credulity had been no match for his art.
Everybody believed her innocent, from the guiltless tenor of her unspotted youth, and from the known libertinism of her barbarous betrayer. Yet her sufferings were too acute for her slender frame; and the same moment that gave birth to her infant, put an end at once to the sorrows and the life of its mother.
The rage of Madame Duval at her elopement, abated not while this injured victim of cruelty yet drew breath. She probably intended, in time, to have pardoned her; but time was not allowed. When she was informed of her death, I have been told, that the agonies of grief and remorse, with which she was seized, occasioned her a severe fit of illness. But, from the time of her recovery to the date of her letter to your Ladyship, I had never heard that she manifested any desire to be made acquainted with the circumstances which attended the death of Lady Belmont, and the birth of her helpless child.
That child, Madam, shall never, while life is lent me, know the loss she has sustained. I have cherished, succoured, and supported her, from her earliest infancy to her sixteenth year; and so amply has she repaid my care and affection, that my fondest wish is now circumscribed by the desire of bestowing her on one who may be sensible of her worth, and then sinking to eternal rest in her arms.
Thus it has happened, that the education of the father, daughter, and granddaughter, has devolved on me. What infinite misery have the two first caused me! Should the fate of the dear survivor be equally adverse, how wretched will be the end of my cares﻿—the end of my days!
Even had Madame Duval merited the charge she claims, I fear my fortitude would have been unequal to such a parting; but being such as she is, not only my affection, but my humanity, recoils, at the barbarous idea of deserting the sacred trust reposed in me.

===Chinese===

——杜瓦尔一家狠辣不饶，他指望的财产落了空；于是他卑鄙地烧掉了两人的婚书，否认他们曾经结过夫妇。
她飞奔到我这里求庇护。再见她时，我心头欢喜与绞痛怎样交并！依我的主意，她设法去寻婚姻的凭证——徒劳；她的轻信，到底不是他奸计的对手。
人人信她清白——凭她无瑕少年的一贯清白，凭她那野蛮负心人出了名的浪荡。然而她的苦太深，她单薄的身子担不起；婴儿呱呱坠地的那一刻，同时了结了母亲的愁苦与性命。
她私奔一事惹起杜瓦尔夫人的狂怒，直到这个横遭摧残的牺牲者咽气，都不曾消减。她多半原打算，来日饶了她；只是没给她来日。闻得她的死讯时——有人告诉我——悲与悔攫住了她，那阵苦痛使她大病一场。可自她病愈直到上书夫人那天，我从未听说她对贝尔蒙特夫人身故和她那孤苦孩子出世的种种情由，流露过半点想知的心。
夫人，只要我一息尚存，那孩子就永远不会知道自己蒙受了怎样的损失。从襁褓到十六岁，我疼她、护她、撑她；而她回报我的照料与慈爱如此丰厚，以至于我如今最大的心愿，只剩把她交付给一个懂得她价值的人，然后在她怀中沉入永息。
事情就这样成了：父亲、女儿、外孙女三代的教养，都落到了我头上。前两位给我造了多大的苦！倘若这亲爱的第三代也遭同样的命，我这操心的结局——我残年的结局——将何等凄惨！
就算杜瓦尔夫人当得起她索要的这份监护，我怕我的坚忍也担不起这样一场分别；何况她是这样一个人——一想到要弃下托付于我的这桩神圣信物，不但我的慈爱，连我的人性，都战栗着退避。

===Original===

Indeed, I could but ill support her former yearly visits to the respectable mansion at Howard Grove: pardon me, dear Madam, and do not think me insensible of the honour which your Ladyship’s condescension confers upon us both; but so deep is the impression which the misfortunes of her mother have made on my heart, that she does not, even for a moment, quit my sight without exciting apprehensions and terrors which almost overpower me. Such, Madam, is my tenderness, and such my weakness!﻿—But she is the only tie I have upon earth, and I trust to your Ladyship’s goodness not to judge of my feelings with severity.
I beg leave to present my humble respects to Mrs. and Miss Mirvan; and have the honour to be,
Madam, your Ladyship’s most obedient

and most humble servant,
Arthur Villars.

===Chinese===

说实在的，就是她往年去霍华德林苑贵府的那些一年一访，我也勉强撑持：原谅我，亲爱的夫人，请勿以为我不知夫人屈尊加于我们祖孙的荣耀；只是她母亲的不幸在我心上刻得太深，她哪怕只离开我一瞬，也会激起几乎将我压倒的忧惧与惊恐。夫人，这便是我的疼爱，这便是我的软弱！——她是我在这世上唯一的系念，我信夫人的仁厚，不至于苛责我这份心情。
请容我向米尔文太太和米尔文小姐敬致卑微的问候；并荣为
夫人您最恭顺、
最卑微的仆人，
阿瑟·维拉尔斯。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

III Lady Howard to the Rev. Mr. Villars
Howard Grove, March 8.
Dear and Rev. Sir,
Your last letter gave me infinite pleasure: after so long and tedious an illness, how grateful to yourself and to your friends must be your returning health! You have the hearty wishes of every individual of this place for its continuance and increase.
Will you not think I take advantage of your acknowledged recovery, if I once more venture to mention your pupil and Howard Grove together? Yet you must remember the patience with which we submitted to your desire of not parting with her during the bad state of your health, though it was with much reluctance we forbore to solicit her company. My granddaughter in particular, has scarce been able to repress her eagerness to again meet the friend of her infancy; and for my own part, it is very strongly my wish to manifest the regard I had for the unfortunate Lady Belmont, by proving serviceable to her child; which seems to me the best respect that can be paid to her memory. Permit me, therefore, to lay before you a plan which Mrs. Mirvan and I have formed, in consequence of your restoration to health.
I would not frighten you;﻿—but do you think you could bear to part with your young companion for two or three months? Mrs. Mirvan proposes to spend the ensuing spring in London, whither for the first time, my grandchild will accompany her: Now, my good friend, it is very earnestly their wish to enlarge and enliven their party by the addition of your amiable ward, who would share, equally with her own daughter, the care and attention of Mrs. Mirvan. Do not start at this proposal; it is time that she should see something of the world. When young people are too rigidly sequestered from it, their lively and romantic imaginations paint it to them as a paradise of which they have been beguiled; but when they are shown it properly, and in due time, they see it such as it really is, equally shared by pain and pleasure, hope and disappointment.
You have nothing to apprehend from her meeting with Sir John Belmont, as that abandoned man is now abroad, and not expected home this year.
Well, my good Sir, what say you to our scheme? I hope it will meet with your approbation; but if it should not, be assured I can never object to any decision of one who is so much respected and esteemed as Mr. Villars, by
His most faithful, humble servant,
M. Howard.

===Chinese===

第三封 霍华德夫人致尊敬的维拉尔斯牧师先生
霍华德林苑，3月8日。
亲爱的、可敬的先生：
您上一封信给了我无限的喜悦：缠绵了这许久的一场病，健康竟然回来了，这对您自己、对您的亲友，是怎样一份感激啊！此间上下每一个人，都诚心祝愿它长驻而且日增。
您既已康复，我又斗胆把您的学生同霍华德林苑一并提起，您会不会觉得我趁人之便？可您总记得，您抱恙期间不愿同她分开，我们忍着多大的不舍，才依了您、没去叨扰她作伴。尤其我的外孙女，她好不容易才按捺住那份急切，盼着再见这位幼年的朋友；至于我自己，我极想把我对那位不幸的贝尔蒙特夫人的敬意，落实为对她的孩子尽一份力——在我看来，这是对她亡灵最好的致敬。因此，请容我把米尔文太太和我——为您康复之故——商定的一个计划，陈在您面前。
我不敢吓您；——可是，同您这位年轻的小伙伴分开两三个月，您觉得还受得住么？米尔文太太打算下一个春天去伦敦，我的外孙女也将头一回随行：那么，我的好朋友，她们极望把您那可爱的被监护人也添进来，好把这支队伍添大些、添热闹些——在米尔文太太那里，她将同亲女儿分享同等的照料与看护。听到这提议别吓一跳：她也到了该见识一点世界的年纪了。年轻人被过严地锁在世界之外时，他们那鲜活而浪漫的想象，会把世界画成一座被骗走了的天堂；可若在适当的时机、以适当的方式引他们看它，他们便看见它本来的样子：苦乐各半，希望与失望均摊。
您不必担心她撞见约翰·贝尔蒙特爵士——那个自暴自弃的人如今在国外，今年料想不会回国。
那么，亲爱的先生，我们的方案您意下如何？望它得您首肯；若不然，也请放心，凡是维拉尔斯先生这样的人所作的决定，我永无异议——他受这样深的敬重与尊崇。我是他
最忠实、最卑微的仆人，
M. 霍华德。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

IV Mr. Villars to Lady Howard
Berry Hill, March 12.
I am grieved, Madam, to appear obstinate, and I blush to incur the imputation of selfishness. In detaining my young charge thus long with myself in the country, I consulted not solely my own inclination. Destined, in all probability, to possess a very moderate fortune, I wished to contract her views to something within it. The mind is but too naturally prone to pleasure, but too easily yielded to dissipation: it has been my study to guard her against their delusions, by preparing her to expect﻿—and to despise them. But the time draws on for experience and observation to take the place of instruction: if I have in some measure, rendered her capable of using one with discretion, and making the other with improvement, I shall rejoice myself with the assurance of having largely contributed to her welfare. She is now of an age that happiness is eager to attend﻿—let her then enjoy it! I commit her to the protection of your Ladyship, and only hope she may be found worthy half the goodness I am satisfied she will meet with at your hospitable mansion.
Thus far, Madam, I cheerfully submit to your desire. In confiding my ward to the care of Lady Howard, I can feel no uneasiness from her absence, but what will arise from the loss of her company, since I shall be as well convinced of her safety as if she were under my own roof.﻿—But can your Ladyship be serious in proposing to introduce her to the gaieties of a London life? Permit me to ask, for what end, or for what purpose? A youthful mind is seldom totally free from ambition; to curb that, is the first step to contentment, since to diminish expectation is to increase enjoyment. I apprehend nothing more than too much raising her hopes and her views, which the natural vivacity of her disposition would render but too easy to effect. The town-acquaintance of Mrs. Mirvan are all in the circle of high life; this artless young creature, with too much beauty to escape notice, has too much sensibility to be indifferent to it; but she has too little wealth to be sought with propriety by men of the fashionable world.
Consider Madam, the peculiar cruelty of her situation.

===Chinese===

第四封 维拉尔斯先生致霍华德夫人
贝里山，3月12日。
夫人，落一个固执的名声，我心里不安；担一个自私的嫌疑，我脸红。我把这年轻的孩子这样久留在乡下身边，考量的并不全是我自己的私愿。她命中十有八九只有一份相当有限的财产，我便想把她的眼界收在限度之内。人心太天然地倾向享乐、太轻易地流于散逸：我多年来用心的，就是让她对那些幻惑有所预备——预备着去期望、也预备着去鄙弃——好护住她。但时候快到了：经验与观察该来接替教诲了。倘若我多少已使她能够审慎地用其一、有进益地取其二，我便可以欣慰地确信：我为她的福祉尽了大力。她正当一个幸福争着来伺候的年纪——那就让她去享吧！我把她托在夫人保护之下，只盼她配得上您府上那份好客的善意的一半——那份善意她会得到多少，我是深信不疑的。
到这里为止，夫人，我都乐于从命。把我的被监护人托给霍华德夫人的照看，她的离开于我不会有什么不安——除了少了她作伴这一桩；因为她的安全，我会确信得同她在自家屋檐下一样。——可是，夫人提议引她见识伦敦生活的欢场，这话是当真的么？请容我问一句：为的是哪个结局、哪个目的？年轻的心很少能全无雄心；管住它，是知足的第一步，因为削减期待就是增添享受。我所忧虑的，莫过于把她的希望和眼界抬得太高——以她天生的活泼性子，这太容易办到了。米尔文太太城里的相识全在上流圈子里；这个不设防的年轻造物，美貌多得躲不开注目，心思又细得不会无动于衷；而她的财产又太少，时髦世界的男人们照规矩是求不得她的。
夫人，请想想她处境里那份特殊的不幸。

===Original===

Only child of a wealthy Baronet, whose person she has never seen, whose character she has reason to abhor, and whose name she is forbidden to claim; entitled as she is to lawfully inherit his fortune and estate, is there any probability that he will *properly* own her? And while he continues to persevere in disavowing his marriage with Miss Evelyn, she shall never, at the expense of her mother’s honour, receive a part of her right as the donation of his bounty.
And as to Mr. Evelyn’s estate, I have no doubt but that Madame Duval and her relations will dispose of it among themselves.
It seems, therefore, as if this deserted child, though legally heiress to two large fortunes, must owe all her rational expectations to adoption and friendship. Yet her income will be such as may make her happy, if she is disposed to be so in private life; though it will by no means allow her to enjoy the luxury of a London fine lady.
Let Miss Mirvan, then, Madam, shine in all the splendour of high life; but suffer my child still to enjoy the pleasures of humble retirement, with a mind to which greater views are unknown.
I hope this reasoning will be honoured with your approbation; and I have yet another motive which has some weight with me: I would not willingly give offence to any human being; and surely Madame Duval might accuse me of injustice, if, while I refuse to let her granddaughter wait upon her, I consent that she should join a party of pleasure to London.
In sending her to Howard Grove, not one of these scruples arise; and therefore Mrs. Clinton, a most worthy woman, formerly her nurse, and now my housekeeper, shall attend her thither next week.
Though I have always called her by the name of Anville, and reported in this neighbourhood that her father, my intimate friend, left her to my guardianship; yet I have thought it necessary she should herself be acquainted with the melancholy circumstances attending her birth: for though I am very desirous of guarding her from curiosity and impertinence, by concealing her name, family, and story, yet I would not leave it in the power of chance to shock her gentle nature with a tale of so much sorrow.

===Chinese===

一位豪富从男爵的独女——他的面她从未见过，他的为人她有理由憎恶，他的姓氏她又不许认领；论法理她有权继承他的财产与产业，可他会*名正言顺地*认她么？而只要他一口咬定不认同伊夫林小姐的婚姻，她就永远不能以牺牲母亲名节为代价，把他的一份恩赏当作她权利的零头收下。
至于伊夫林先生的产业，我不怀疑，杜瓦尔夫人和她的亲眷们会自行分掉。
所以，这个被弃的孩子，虽然按法律是两份大宗家产的继承人，她一切现实的指望，却只好寄于收养与情谊。不过她的进项也够她在平民生活里过快活日子——只要她安于那样；却断断不够她享受一位伦敦时鬓名媛的排场。
那么，夫人，让米尔文小姐去在上流的光辉里熠熠生辉吧；只求容我这孩子，继续享受寒微乡居的清福——带着一颗不识更大图谋的心。
我希望这番道理能蒙夫人嘉许；我还有一层动机，也有些分量：我不愿开罪世上任何人；而我若一面拒绝让她的外孙女去伺候她，一面却同意这孩子加入去伦敦游乐的一伙，杜瓦尔夫人准会指责我不公。
送她去霍华德林苑，这些顾虑一条也不沾；因此克林顿太太（Mrs. Clinton）——一位极可敬的妇人，从前她的乳母，如今我的管家——下星期将陪她前往。
虽说我一直只叫她安维尔（Anville），并对左近乡邻说，她父亲——我的挚友——把她托给了我监护；可我认定，她本人必须知道随她出世而来的那桩伤心事的原委：因为我固然极想靠隐去她的姓名、家世和来历，护她免遭好奇与唐突，可我也不肯把这样一段浸满悲伤的故事，留给机缘去向她那温柔的天性当头一击。

===Original===

You must not, Madam, expect too much from my pupil; she is quite a little rustic, and knows nothing of the world; and though her education has been the best I could bestow in this retired place, to which Dorchester, the nearest town, is seven miles distant, yet I shall not be surprised if you should discover in her a thousand deficiencies of which I have never dreamt. She must be very much altered since she was last at Howard Grove. But I will say nothing of her; I leave her to your Ladyship’s own observations, of which I beg a faithful relation; and am,
Dear Madam,

with great respect,

Your obedient and most humble Servant,
Arthur Villars.

===Chinese===

夫人，对我的学生不可期望太高；她十足是个小村姑，于世事一无所知；她受的教育，已是我在这僻地所能给的最好——从这里到最近的镇子多切斯特也有七英里——可您若在她身上发现一千样我做梦也没想到的欠缺，我也不会吃惊。自她上次来霍华德林苑后，她想必变了许多。关于她，我不多说了；把她留给夫人亲自观察，并恳请如实相告；我是
亲爱的夫人，

怀着深深敬意的

您恭顺而卑微的仆人，
阿瑟·维拉尔斯。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

V Mr. Villars to Lady Howard
March 18.
Dear Madam,
This letter will be delivered to you by my child﻿—the child of my adoption﻿—my affection! Unblest with one natural friend, she merits a thousand. I send her to you innocent as an angel, and artless as purity itself; and I send you with her the heart of your friend, the only hope he has on earth, the subject of his tenderest thoughts, and the object of his latest cares. She is one, Madam, for whom alone I have lately wished to live; and she is one whom to serve I would with transport die! Restore her but to me all innocence as you receive her, and the fondest hope of my heart will be amply gratified.
A. Villars.

===Chinese===

第五封 维拉尔斯先生致霍华德夫人
3月18日。
亲爱的夫人：
这封信将由我的孩子——我收养的孩子——我的宝贝——亲自呈上！她没有一个血亲眷友，却配得上一千个。我把她送到您那里：天真如天使，坦荡如纯洁本身；随她同去的，还有您朋友的心——他在世上仅剩的希望，他心头最温柔的念想，他残年最后的心事。夫人，她是我近来唯一愿意为之活下去的人，也是我甘愿欢欢喜喜为之效劳而死的人！只要您把她还给我时，同您接她时一样天真无瑕，我心底最深的爱便得偿所愿。
A. 维拉尔斯。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

VI Lady Howard to the Rev. Mr. Villars
Howard Grove.
Dear Rev. Sir,
The solemn manner in which you have committed your child to my care, has in some measure damped the pleasure which I receive from the trust, as it makes me fear that you suffer from your compliance, in which case I shall very sincerely blame myself for the earnestness with which I have requested this favour: but remember, my good Sir, she is within a few days summons; and be assured, I will not detain her a moment longer than you wish.
You desire my opinion of her.
She is a little angel! I cannot wonder that you sought to monopolize her: neither ought you, at finding it impossible.
Her face and person answer my most refined ideas of complete beauty: and this, though a subject of praise less important to you, or, to me than any other, is yet so striking, it is not possible to pass it unnoticed. Had I not known from whom she received her education, I should at first sight of so perfect a face, have been in pain for her understanding; since it has been long and justly remarked, that folly has ever sought alliance with beauty.
She has the same gentleness in her manners, the same natural graces in her motions, that I formerly so much admired in her mother. Her character seems truly ingenuous and simple; and at the same time that nature has blessed her with an excellent understanding and great quickness of parts, she has a certain air of inexperience and innocency that is extremely interesting.
You have not reason to regret the retirement in which she has lived; since that politeness which is acquired by an acquaintance with high life, is in her so well supplied by a natural desire of obliging, joined to a deportment infinitely engaging.
I observe, with great satisfaction, a growing affection between this amiable girl and my granddaughter, whose heart is as free from selfishness or conceit, as that of her young friend is from all guile. Their regard may be mutually useful, since much is to be expected from emulation where nothing is to be feared from envy. I would have them love each other as sisters, and reciprocally supply the place of that tender and happy relationship to which neither of them has a natural claim.
Be satisfied, my good Sir, that your child shall meet with the same attention as our own.

===Chinese===

第六封 霍华德夫人致尊敬的维拉尔斯牧师先生
霍华德林苑。
亲爱的、可敬的先生：
您把孩子托付给我时那副郑重的神情，倒把我从这桩信托中得的喜悦压低了几分——它让我担心，您这番俯就实是出于勉强；果真如此，那我要为自己的恳切请求，真心真意地怪自己了：可是记住，我的好先生，她只在几日之遥的地方，一召即至；而且请您放心，您什么时候要她回去，我一刻也不多留。
您要我谈谈对她的看法。
她是位小天使！难怪您一心想把她独占：也不必奇怪，这终究独占不成。
她的容貌与身段，正合我关于十全之美最精微的想头；这一层虽不是您我眼里头一等要紧的夸赞，却实在太打眼，想略过不提都不成。倘若我不知她受教于何人，乍见这样一张完美无缺的脸，我倒要先替她的头脑担心了——因为长久以来人皆公论：愚憨向与美貌攀亲。
她的举止同她母亲当年一样温婉，一举一动有同一样的天然风致。她的性子真是坦白简易；而造物既赋了她一副极好的悟性和极敏捷的天分，又给她笼上一层不谙世事、一片天真的气韵，格外动人。
您无须惋惜她一向深居简出：上流社会中习得的那份文雅，她已由一种天然愿人欢喜的心性，加上无限可亲的仪态，补得足足的了。
我以极大的快慰看着这位可爱的姑娘同我外孙女日浓一日地亲爱；外孙女的心同她这位小朋友的心一样——一个全无自私与自矜，一个全无半点狡猾。她俩的情谊彼此都有益处：既无须妒忌之惧，相竞之效便大可期待。我愿她们像亲姐妹一样相爱，彼此补上那份谁也没福气天生领有的温柔亲缘。
我的好先生，请您放心：您的孩子会受到同我们自己孩子一样的照拂。

===Original===

We all join in most hearty wishes for your health and happiness, and in returning our sincere thanks for the favour you have conferred on us.
I am, dear Sir,

Your most faithful servant,
M. Howard.

===Chinese===

我们全家一起，最诚挚地祝您康健安乐，并为您惠然赐予我们的这份恩情，回以致谢。
我是，亲爱的先生，

您最忠实的仆人，
M. 霍华德。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

VII Lady Howard to the Rev. Mr. Villars
Howard Grove, March 26.
Be not alarmed, my worthy friend, at my so speedily troubling you again; I seldom use the ceremony of waiting for answers, or writing with any regularity, and I have at present immediate occasion for begging your patience.
Mrs. Mirvan has just received a letter from her long absent husband, containing the welcome news of his hoping to reach London by the beginning of next week. My daughter and the Captain have been separated almost seven years, and it would therefore be needless to say what joy, surprise, and consequently confusion, his at present unexpected return has caused at Howard Grove. Mrs. Mirvan, you cannot doubt, will go instantly to town to meet him; her daughter is under a thousand obligations to attend her; I grieve that her mother cannot.
And now, my good Sir, I almost blush to proceed;﻿—but, tell me, may I ask﻿—will you permit﻿—that your child may accompany them? Do not think us unreasonable, but consider the many inducements which conspire to make London the happiest place at present she can be in. The joyful occasion of the journey; the gaiety of the whole party, opposed to the dull life she must lead, if left here with a solitary old woman for her sole companion, while she so well knows the cheerfulness and felicity enjoyed by the rest of the family﻿—are circumstances that seem to merit your consideration. Mrs. Mirvan desires me to assure you that one week is all she asks, as she is certain that the Captain, who hates London, will be eager to revisit Howard Grove; and Maria is so very earnest in wishing to have the company of her friend, that, if you are inexorable, she will be deprived of half the pleasure she otherwise hopes to receive.
However, I will not, my good Sir, deceive you into an opinion that they intend to live in a retired manner, as that cannot be fairly expected. But you have no reason to be uneasy concerning Madame Duval; she has not any correspondent in England, and obtains no intelligence but by common report. She must be a stranger to the name your child bears; and, even should she hear of this excursion, so short a time as a week or less spent in town upon so particular an occasion, though previous to their meeting, cannot be construed into disrespect to herself.
Mrs.

===Chinese===

第七封 霍华德夫人致尊敬的维拉尔斯牧师先生
霍华德林苑，3月26日。
我的好朋友，别惊慌，我又这么快来搅扰您；我向来不讲究等回信的礼数，写信也没有个定规，眼下更是立刻就要劳驾您的耐心了。
米尔文太太刚收到她久别的丈夫一封信，带来可喜的消息：他指望下星期初抵达伦敦。我女儿同这位舰长分离已近七年，他这趟出乎意料的归来，在霍华德林苑激起怎样的欢喜、惊奇、随之而来的忙乱，也就不必多说了。米尔文太太——这您毋庸怀疑——必将即刻进城相迎；她的女儿有一千个理由随行；可叹她的母亲不能同去。
而现在，我的好先生，我几乎羞于启齿；——可是告诉我，我能不能问——您可容许——容您的孩子随她们同去？别当我们不讲道理，只求您想想那许多凑在一处的缘由，怎样使伦敦成为她眼下最能得到快乐的地方。此行有喜事作由头；一伙人欢欢喜喜——同她若被留下、只能陪一个孤零零的老太婆作伴的那种闷日子，两相对照——而家里其余人正享着怎样的热闹与快活，她又知道得清清楚楚——这些情形，似乎都值得您斟酌。米尔文太太要我向您保证：她只求一个星期，因为她确信舰长厌恶伦敦，必然急着回霍华德林苑来；玛丽亚又那样一心盼着有她朋友作伴，您若铁面不肯，她这趟能指望的一半乐趣就要被剥夺了。
不过，我的好先生，我不愿欺骗您，让你们以为她们打算深居简出——这实在指望不来。但您不必为杜瓦尔夫人担心：她在英格兰没有一个通信的人，消息只凭市井传闻。您孩子用的名字，她必然隔膜；即便她听说这趟出行，为着这样一桩特殊的缘由进城，逗留不过一星期甚至更短，又赶在两人会面之前，也断不至于被说成对她的不敬。
米尔文

===Original===

Mirvan desires me to assure you, that if you will oblige her, her *two* children shall equally share her time and her attention. She has sent a commission to a friend in town to take a house for her; and while she waits for an answer concerning it, I shall for one from you to our petition. However, your child is writing herself; and that, I doubt not, will more avail than all we can possible urge.
My daughter desires her best compliments to you *if*, she says, you will grant her request but *not else*.
Adieu, my dear Sir, we all hope everything from your goodness.
M. Howard.

===Chinese===

太太还要我向您保证：您若肯俯允，她的*两个*孩子将均分她的时间和看护。她已托城里一位朋友代为觅宅；在等那边的回音时，我便等您对我们这纸请愿的回音。况且，您的孩子正亲自给您写信呢；我毫不怀疑，那封信比我们所能进言的一切都更管用。
我女儿向您致意——她说，*如果您*答应她的请求；*不然就不*问候了。
再会，亲爱的先生，我们把一切指望都寄托在您的仁厚上。
M. 霍华德。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

VIII Evelina to the Rev. Mr. Villars
Howard Grove, March 26.
This house seems to be the house of joy; every face wears a smile, and a laugh is at everybody’s service. It is quite amusing to walk about and see the general confusion; a room leading to the garden is fitting up for Captain Mirvan’s study. Lady Howard does not sit a moment in a place; Miss Mirvan is making caps; everybody so busy!﻿—such flying from room to room!﻿—so many orders given, and retracted, and given again! nothing but hurry and perturbation.
Well but, my dear Sir, I am desired to make a request to you. I hope you will not think me an encroacher; Lady Howard insists upon my writing!﻿—yet I hardly know how to go on; a petition implies a want and have you left me one? No, indeed.
I am half ashamed of myself for beginning this letter. But these dear ladies are so pressing﻿—I cannot, for my life, resist wishing for the pleasures they offer me﻿—provided you do not disapprove them.
They are to make a very short stay in town. The Captain will meet them in a day or two. Mrs. Mirvan and her sweet daughter both go; what a happy party! Yet, I am not *very* eager to accompany them: at least I shall be contented to remain where I am, if you desire that I should.
Assured, my dearest Sir, of your goodness, your bounty, and your indulgent kindness, ought I to form a wish that has not your sanction? Decide for me, therefore, without the least apprehension that I shall be uneasy or discontented. While I am yet in suspense, perhaps I may *hope*; but I am most certain that when you have once determined I shall not repine.
They tell me that London is now in full splendour. Two playhouses are open﻿—the Opera-house﻿—Ranelagh﻿—and the Pantheon.﻿—You see I have learned all their names. However, pray don’t suppose that I make any point of going, for I shall hardly sigh, to see them depart without me, though I shall probably never meet with such another opportunity. And, indeed, their domestic happiness will be so great﻿—it is natural to wish to partake of it.
I believe I am bewitched! I made a resolution, when I began, that I would not be urgent; but my pen﻿—or rather my thoughts, will not suffer me to keep it﻿—for I acknowledge, I must acknowledge, I cannot help wishing for your permission.

===Chinese===

第八封 伊芙琳娜致尊敬的维拉尔斯牧师先生
霍华德林苑，3月26日。
这座宅子眼下简直是座欢喜之宫；每一张脸都挂着笑，笑声随取随用。在各处走一走、看看那普遍的忙乱，真是有趣：一间通花园的屋子正在布置，要作米尔文舰长的书房。霍华德夫人一刻也坐不住；米尔文小姐在做的帽子；人人都这样忙！——这样满屋子飞！——这样多的吩咐，收回了又吩咐，吩咐了又收回！除了匆忙与忙乱，再没有别的。
可是，亲爱的先生，他们要我向您提一个请求。但愿您别当我得寸进尺；是霍华德夫人一定要我写！——可我简直不知怎样落笔：请愿意味着有所缺，而您可曾让我缺过什么？没有，真的没有。
起了这个头，我已有点羞自己。可是这几位亲爱的太太小姐这样催——我实在没法子，不想往她们递来的欢乐——只要您不以为非。
她们在城里只作极短的逗留。舰长一两天内就同她们会合。米尔文太太和她那可爱的女儿都去；多快乐的一伙！然而我并不*十分*急着随行：至少，您若要我留下，我留在原地也是心安的。
我最亲爱的先生，您的仁善、您的慷慨、您那宽容的慈爱，我既深信不疑，我难道还该怀一个未经您首肯的愿吗？所以，请您替我定夺，完全不必担心我会不痛快、会气闷。此刻悬而未决，我或许还会*指望*；可您一旦定了，我断不会再嘀咕，这一点我最清楚不过。
她们告诉我，伦敦眼下正是一年中最光彩的时节。两家戏院都开着——还有歌剧院——拉内拉夫——还有万神殿。——您瞧，这些名字我全学会了。不过请您千万别以为我非去不可；她们不带我走，我目送时是几乎不会叹气的——虽然这样的机会，我这一生怕是再遇不上第二个了。况且，他们一家团圆的那份幸福会那样浓——想沾一份，也是人之常情呀。
我怕是中了魔了！下笔时我本打定主意，绝不苦苦恳求；可我这管笔——不如说我这颗心，不肯让我守约——因为我承认，我必须承认，我禁不住盼您点头。

===Original===

I almost repent already that I have made this confession; pray forget that you have read it, if this journey is displeasing to you. But I will not write any longer; for the more I think of this affair, the less indifferent to it I find myself.
Adieu, my most honoured, most reverenced, most beloved father! for by what other name can I call you? I have no happiness or sorrow, no hope or fear, but what your kindness bestows, or your displeasure may cause. You will not, I am sure, send a refusal without reasons unanswerable, and therefore I shall cheerfully acquiesce. Yet I hope﻿—I hope you will be able to permit me to go!
I am, with the utmost affection,

gratitude, and duty, your
Evelina —﻿—﻿—
I cannot to *you* sign **Anville**, and what other name may I claim?

===Chinese===

话已招认，我已几乎后悔；这趟出行若不中您的意，就请忘掉您读到的这些。可我不再写下去了；这件事越想，我越发现自己越做不到不在乎。
再会，我最敬爱、最尊崇、最亲的父亲！——除了父亲，我还能用哪个名字叫您呢？我没有一分快乐或忧伤、一分希望或忧惧，不来自您的慈爱、不系于您的不悦。我知道，您绝不会不给出无可辩驳的理由就回绝，所以无论如何我都会欣然顺从。可是我还是盼——盼您能准我去！
我怀着最深的爱、感激与孝敬，是您的
伊芙琳娜——
对*您*，我签不出**安维尔**这个名字；而别的名字，我又有什么可签的呢？

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

IX Mr. Villars to Evelina
Berry Hill, March 28.
To resist the urgency of entreaty, is a power which I have not yet acquired: I aim not at an authority which deprives you of liberty, yet I would fain guide myself by a prudence which should save me the pangs of repentance. Your impatience to fly to a place which your imagination has painted to you in colors so attractive, surprises me not; I have only to hope, that the liveliness of your fancy may not deceive you: to refuse, would be raising it still higher. To see my Evelina happy, is to see myself without a wish: go then, my child; and may that Heaven, which alone can direct, preserve and strengthen you! To that, my love, will I daily offer prayers for your felicity. O may it guard, watch over you, defend you from danger, save you from distress, and keep vice as distant from your person as from your heart! And to me, may it grant, the ultimate blessing of closing these aged eyes in the arms of one so dear﻿—so deservedly beloved!
Arthur Villars.

===Chinese===

第九封 维拉尔斯先生致伊芙琳娜
贝里山，3月28日。
拒绝恳切的哀求，这门本领我至今没有学会；我无意追求一种剥夺你自由的权威，却也想凭一份审慎行事，免得日后受悔恨的咬啮。你急欲飞向一个被你的想象涂得那样鲜妍的地方，这不叫我意外；我只盼，你想象的鲜活莫要骗了你：若是回绝，只会把那地方涂得更高。看见我的伊芙琳娜快乐，便等于看见我一无所求；那么去吧，我的孩子；愿那唯有它能指引的上天，保佑你、扶持你！我的爱，我要每日为你的幸福祈祷于它。哦，愿它守护你、看顾你，救你脱于危难、免于困苦，叫恶远远地离开你的身，如同离开你的心！至于我，愿它赐我那最后的一福：让我这双老眼，阖在这样亲爱、这样值得敬爱的一条臂弯里！
阿瑟·维拉尔斯。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

X Evelina to the Rev. Mr. Villars
Queen Ann Street, London, Saturday, April 2.
This moment arrived. Just going to Drury Lane Theatre. The celebrated Mr. Garrick performs Ranger. I am quite in ecstasy. So is Miss Mirvan. How fortunate that he should happen to play! We would not let Mrs. Mirvan rest till she consented to go. Her chief objection was to our dress, for we have had no time to *Londonize* ourselves; but we teased her into compliance, and so we are to sit in some obscure place that she may not be seen. As to me, I should be alike unknown in the most conspicuous or most private part of the house.
I can write no more now. I have hardly time to breathe﻿—only just this, the houses and streets are not quite so superb as I expected. However, I have seen nothing yet, so I ought not to judge.
Well; adieu, my dearest Sir, for the present; I could not forbear writing a few words instantly on my arrival, though I suppose my letter of thanks for your consent is still on the road.
Saturday Night.
O, my dear Sir, in what raptures am I returned? Well may Mr. Garrick be so celebrated, so universally admired﻿—I had not any idea of so great a performer.
Such ease! such vivacity in his manner! such grace in his motions! such fire and meaning in his eyes!﻿—I could hardly believe he had studied a written part, for every word seemed to be uttered from the impulse of the moment.
His action﻿—at once so graceful and so free!﻿—his voice﻿—so clear, so melodious, yet so wonderfully various in its tones!﻿—Such animation!﻿—every look *speaks*!
I would have given the world to have had the whole play acted over again. And when he danced﻿—O, how I envied Clarinda! I almost wished to have jumped on the stage and joined them.
I am afraid you will think me mad, so I won’t say any more; yet, I really believe Mr. Garrick would make you mad too if you could see him. I intend to ask Mrs. Mirvan to go to the play every night while we stay in town. She is extremely kind to me; and Maria, her charming daughter, is the sweetest girl in the world.
I shall write to you every evening all that passes in the day, and that in the same manner as, if I could see, I should tell you.
Sunday.
This morning we went to Portland Chapel; and afterwards we walked in the mall of St.

===Chinese===

第十封 伊芙琳娜致尊敬的维拉尔斯牧师先生
伦敦，女王安妮街，星期六，4月2日。
此刻刚刚到。马上要去特鲁里街剧院。大名鼎鼎的加里克先生演"游侠"兰杰。我简直欣喜若狂。米尔文小姐也一样。他碰巧登台，多运气！我们缠着米尔文太太不肯罢休，直到她答应去。她主要的顾虑是我们这身衣裳——我们还来不及把自己*伦敦化*呢；可我们把她磨得依了我们，所以我们得坐在某个僻静的角落，免得被熟人看见。至于我，坐全场最打眼的地方同最角落的地方一样没人认得。
现在写不下去了。气都透不过来——只说这一句：房子和街道并不如我想的那么堂皇。不过我什么都还没看，还不该下判断。
好；暂时再会，我最亲爱的先生；一到就忍不住写上这几行，虽然我猜想，我那封谢您允准的信还在路上呢。
星期六夜里。
哦，亲爱的先生，我是怀着怎样的狂喜回来的！加里克先生名满天下、人人倾倒，难怪——这样了不起的演员，我从前竟毫无概念。
做派那样自在！那样生气勃勃！举止那样优雅！眼睛里那样的火和意思！——我几乎不能相信他演的是写好的本子，每个字都像当场从心里迸出来的。
他的动作——既优雅又洒脱！——他的嗓音——又清亮，又悦耳，腔调又变化得那样神妙！——那样神采飞扬！——每一个眼神*都会说话*！
要是能把整出戏重演一遍，让我拿全世界换我都肯。他跳舞的时候——哦，我多羡慕克拉琳达！我几乎想跳上台去，同他们一起跳。
恐怕您要当我疯了，那我就不多说了；可是我真的相信，您若能看他一眼，加里克先生也会把您弄疯的。我打算求米尔文太太，我们在城里期间每晚都去看戏。她待我极其亲厚；玛丽亚，她那可爱的女儿，是天底下最甜的姑娘。
我要每晚给您写信，把白天的一切都写给您——就同我能当面见您时那样讲给您听。
星期日。
今晨我们去了波特兰礼拜堂；随后在圣

===Original===

James’s Park, which by no means answered my expectations: it is a long straight walk of dirty gravel, very uneasy to the feet; and at each end instead of an open prospect, nothing is to be seen but houses built of brick. When Mrs. Mirvan pointed out the *Palace* to me﻿—I think I was never much more surprised.
However, the walk was very agreeable to us; everybody looked gay, and seemed pleased; and the ladies were so much dressed, that Miss Mirvan and I could do nothing but look at them. Mrs. Mirvan met several of her friends. No wonder, for I never saw so many people assembled together before. I looked about for some of *my* acquaintance, but in vain; for I saw not one person that I knew, which is very odd, for all the world seemed there.
Mrs. Mirvan says we are not to walk in the Park again next Sunday, even if we should be in town, because there is better company in Kensington Gardens; but really if you had seen how much everybody was dressed, you would not think that possible.
Monday.
We are to go this evening to a private ball, given by Mrs. Stanley, a very fashionable lady of Mrs. Mirvan’s acquaintance.
We have been *a-shopping* as Mrs. Mirvan calls it, all this morning, to buy silks, caps, gauzes, and so forth.
The shops are really very entertaining, especially the mercers; there seem to be six or seven men belonging to each shop; and every one took care by bowing and smirking, to be noticed. We were conducted from one to another, and carried from room to room with so much ceremony, that at first I was almost afraid to go on.
I thought I should never have chosen a silk: for they produced so many, I knew not which to fix upon; and they recommended them all so strongly, that I fancy they thought I only wanted persuasion to buy everything they showed me. And, indeed, they took so much trouble, that I was almost ashamed I could not.
At the milliners, the ladies we met were so much dressed, that I should rather have imagined they were making visits than purchases. But what most diverted me was, that we were more frequently served by men than by women; and such men! so finical, so affected! they seemed to understand every part of a woman’s dress better than we do ourselves; and they recommended caps and ribbons with an air of so much importance, that I wished to ask them how long they had left off wearing them.

===Chinese===

詹姆斯公园的林荫道里散步——这地方全不合我的期望：一条又长又直的碎石路，泥乎乎的，硌得脚疼；两头不是开阔的景色，能望见的只有一排排砖房。米尔文太太指给我看那座*王宫*时——我想我从没这么吃惊过。
不过这趟散步还是很有意趣；人人面带欢容，个个喜气洋洋；太太们穿戴得那样盛，米尔文小姐同我除了看她们，什么都做不了。米尔文太太遇见了好几位朋友。难怪，我从没见过这么多的人聚在一处。我四下里找*我*认识的人，徒劳；一个人也不认得，这真怪，全世界好像都在这儿了。
米尔文太太说，下个星期日就算我们还在城里，也不去这个公园了，因为肯辛顿花园里的体面人更多；可是说真的，您要是见了人人穿戴得那个样子，准会觉得这不可能。
星期一。
今晚我们要去一场私家舞会，斯坦利夫人办的——米尔文太太的一位极时髦的朋友。
我们逛了一上午街——照米尔文太太的说法，*逛铺子*——买绸子、帽子、纱，等等。
这些铺子真有看头，绸缎铺尤其；每家铺子里似乎都有六七个伙计，个个鞠躬、递笑脸，惟恐人不注意他。我们被人从一位引到另一位，从一间屋子让到另一间屋子，礼数那样多，起初我几乎不敢往前走。
我差一点挑不中一块绸子：他们拿出来的太多了，我不知定哪一块好；他们又把每一块都说得那样好，我猜想他们以为我只差一句劝，就会把他们拿出来的全买下。说真的，他们费了那么多事，我几乎为自己买不下而羞愧。
在女帽铺里，遇见的太太们穿戴得太盛，我倒以为她们是来拜客，不是来买东西的。可最逗我的是，给我们张罗的常常是男人，不是女人；而且是那样的男人！那样娇气，那样作态！女人衣装的每一处，他们仿佛比我们自己还懂；他们荐帽子、荐缎带时那副郑重其事的气派，我真想问问他们：搁下不戴这些，已经多少年了？

===Original===

The dispatch with which they work in these great shops is amazing, for they have promised me a complete suit of linen against the evening.
I have just had my hair dressed. You can’t think how oddly my head feels; full of powder and black pins, and a great cushion on the top of it. I believe you would hardly know me, for my face looks quite different to what it did before my hair was dressed. When I shall be able to make use of a comb for myself I cannot tell; for my hair is so much entangled, *frizzled* they call it, that I fear it will be very difficult.
I am half afraid of this ball tonight; for, you know, I have never danced but at school: however, Miss Mirvan says there is nothing in it. Yet, I wish it was over.
Adieu, my dear Sir, pray excuse the wretched stuff I write; perhaps I may improve by being in this town, and then my letters will be less unworthy your reading. Meantime, I am,
Your dutiful and affectionate,

though unpolished,
Evelina.
Poor Miss Mirvan cannot wear one of the caps she made, because they dress her hair too large for them.

===Chinese===

这些大铺子里做事的快当真了不得：他们答应我傍晚以前备齐一整套内衣。
我刚做完了头发。您想不到我脑袋现在多别扭：满头发粉和黑发夹，顶上还髻着一大只垫子。我想您准认不出我了——做过头发，我的脸同先前全然两样。什么时候我才能自己使得动梳子，我说不上来；头发缠得那样厉害——他们管那叫*卷花*——我怕是很难梳开了。
今晚这舞会，我有点心虚；您知道的，我除了在学校，从没跳过舞：不过米尔文小姐说没什么难的。可我巴不得它已经过去了。
再会，亲爱的先生，请原谅我写得这样糟糕；住在这个城里我兴许会进步，那时我的信就不至于这样有污尊目了。 在此期间，我是您孝顺而亲爱的、
虽然粗拙的
伊芙琳娜。
可怜的米尔文小姐一顶自己做的帽子也戴不成，因为头发做得太大，帽子扣不上了。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

XI Evelina in Continuation
Queen Ann Street, April 5, Tuesday Morning.
I have a vast deal to say, and shall give all this morning to my pen.
As to my plan of writing every evening the adventures of the day, I find it impracticable; for the diversions here are so very late, that if I begin my letters after them, I could not go to bed at all.
We passed a most extraordinary evening. A *private* ball this was called, so I expected to have seen about four or five couple; but Lord! my dear Sir, I believe I saw half the world! Two very large rooms were full of company; in one were cards for the elderly ladies, and in the other were the dancers. My mamma Mirvan, for she always calls me her child, said she would sit with Maria and me till we were provided with partners, and then join the cardplayers.
The gentlemen, as they passed and repassed, looked as if they thought we were quite at their disposal, and only waiting for the honour of their commands; and they sauntered about, in a careless, indolent manner, as if with a view to keep us in suspense. I don’t speak of this in regard to Miss Mirvan and myself only, but to the ladies in general: and I thought it so provoking, that I determined in my own mind that, far from humouring such airs, I would rather not dance at all, than with anyone who would seem to think me ready to accept the first partner who would condescend to take me.
Not long after, a young man, who had for some time looked at us with a kind of negligent impertinence, advanced on tiptoe towards me; he had a set smile on his face, and his dress was so foppish, that I really believed he even wished to be stared at; and yet he was very ugly.
Bowing almost to the ground with a sort of swing, and waving his hand, with the greatest conceit, after a short and silly pause, he said, “Madam﻿—may I presume?”﻿—and stopped, offering to take my hand. I drew it back, but could scarce forbear laughing. “Allow me, Madam,” continued he, affectedly breaking off every half moment, “the honour and happiness﻿—if I am not so unhappy as to address you too late﻿—to have the happiness and honour﻿—”
Again he would have taken my hand; but bowing my head, I begged to be excused, and turned to Miss Mirvan to conceal my laughter. He then desired to know if I had already engaged myself to some more fortunate man? I said No, and that I believed I should not dance at all.

===Chinese===

第十一封 伊芙琳娜续
女王安妮街，4月5日，星期二早晨。
我有满肚子的话要说，这一上午全交给笔了。
原打算每晚把当天的奇遇写给您，发现行不通：这里的消遣收场得太晚，等散了场再写信，那就干脆不用睡了。
我们过了一个非同寻常的晚上。这场舞会称作*私家*舞会，所以我原以为不过四五对宾客；可是老天爷！亲爱的先生，我怕是见到了半个世界！两大间屋子全坐满了：一间里年长的太太们打牌，另一间里是跳舞的。我的米尔文妈妈——她总把我叫她的孩子——说，她先陪玛丽亚和我坐着，等我们有了舞伴，再去入局打牌。
先生们走来又走去，那副神气仿佛我们全凭他们发落，只等着叨光领他们的吩咐；他们又那样散漫拖沓地晃来晃去，像成心吊着我们的胃口。这我不是单说米尔文小姐和我，是说全体女士：我觉得太气人了，心里拿定主意——这样的架子万万迎合不得，宁可整晚不跳，也决不同任何一个、看着像以为我正巴不得谁来屈尊拣我就行的人跳。
没多久，一个年轻人朝我们踱了过来——他先前一直用一种懒洋洋的冒失劲儿打量我们。他踮着脚尖，脸上挂着一份挤出来的笑，衣裳穿得那样浮华，我简直相信他就盼着人盯他看；可他又实在丑。
他带着一种摇荡的派头几乎一躬到地，又极其自命不凡地挥一挥手，愣了半晌的傻停顿，才说："夫人——我可以冒昧么？"——说着停住，伸手要拉我的手。我抽了回来，可几乎憋不住笑。"请赏光，夫人，"他接下去，每半句话做作地断一回，"这份荣幸与福气——倘若我不至于不幸到开口太迟——能得这份福气与荣幸——"
他又来拉我的手；我点了点头，告了个罪，扭过脸对着米尔文小姐掩住笑。他便问，我是不是已经答应了哪位更幸运的先生？我说没有，又说我看今晚索性不跳了。

===Original===

He would keep himself he told me, disengaged, in hopes I should relent; and then, uttering some ridiculous speeches of sorrow and disappointment, though his face still wore the same invariable smile, he retreated.
It so happened, as we have since recollected, that during this little dialogue Mrs. Mirvan was conversing with the lady of the house. And very soon after, another gentleman, who seemed about six-and-twenty years old, gaily but not foppishly dressed, and indeed extremely handsome, with an air of mixed politeness and gallantry, desired to know if I was engaged, or would honour him with my hand. So he was pleased to say, though I am sure I know not what honour he could receive from me; but these sort of expressions, I find, are used as words of course, without any distinction of persons, or study of propriety.
Well, I bowed, and I am sure I coloured; for indeed I was frightened at the thoughts of dancing before so many people, all strangers, and, which was worse, *with* a stranger: however, that was unavoidable; for, though I looked round the room several times, I could not see one person that I knew. And so he took my hand, and led me to join in the dance.
The minuets were over before we arrived, for we were kept late by the milliners making us wait for our things.
He seemed very desirous of entering into conversation with me; but I was seized with such a panic, that I could hardly speak a word, and nothing but the shame of so soon changing my mind prevented my returning to my seat, and declining to dance at all.
He appeared to be surprised at my terror, which I believe was but too apparent: however, he asked no questions, though I fear he must think it very strange, for I did not choose to tell him it was owing to my never before dancing but with a schoolgirl.
His conversation was sensible and spirited; his air, and address were open and noble; his manners gentle, attentive, and infinitely engaging; his person is all elegance, and his countenance the most animated and expressive I have ever seen.
In a short time we were joined by Miss Mirvan, who stood next couple to us. But how I was startled when she whispered me that my partner was a nobleman! This gave me a new alarm: how will he be provoked, thought I, when he finds what a simple rustic he has honoured with his choice!

===Chinese===

他说他就不跳了，留着空当，巴望我回心转意；接着说了几句又可笑又丧气的抱憾之辞——脸上却始终挂着那副一成不变的笑——退了下去。
事后我们回想起来，这段小小的对答进行时，米尔文太太恰在同女主人聊天。很快，另一位先生走了过来：看去二十六七岁，衣装鲜亮而不浮华，人其实极英俊，一派文雅与殷勤兼有的气度；他请问，我可有舞伴，能否赏他一臂之劳。他是这样客气说的——虽然我确实不明白，我能给他什么光荣；可我发现，这类辞令是照例的套话，不分对象，也不论合不合宜。
好吧，我屈了屈膝，脸也红了；想到要在这么多全然陌生的人面前跳舞——更糟的是，还*同一个*陌生人跳——我实在是怕；可这没法躲开：房间里我张望了好几遍，一个人也不认得。于是他执了我的手，领我入了舞列。
我们到时小步舞已经跳完了——都被女帽铺子拖着，等东西误了时辰。
他像是极想同我攀谈；可我慌得一句话也说不出，若不是马上改口太丢人，我几乎要退回座位，索性不跳了。
他见我害怕，似乎吃了一惊——我怕那样子也太明显了；不过他没有问什么，虽然他多半觉得蹊跷，因为我没肯告诉他：这是因为我从前除了同女同学，从没跳过舞。
他的谈吐明白而有生气；风度言辞开朗高贵；举止温文、体贴，无限可亲；身段通体优雅，那副面容是我生平所见最生动、最富表情的。
不多时，米尔文小姐加入了我们，就站我们邻对。可她咬耳朵告诉我，我的舞伴是位勋爵时，我吓了一跳！这给了我新的惊慌：等他发现，他屈尊选中的原来是个多土的乡巴佬，他会多恼——一个因为不谙世事、时时刻刻怕做错事的人！

===Original===

one whose ignorance of the world makes her perpetually fear doing something wrong!
That he should be so much my superior in every way, quite disconcerted me; and you will suppose my spirits were not much raised, when I heard a lady, in passing us, say, “This is the most difficult dance I ever saw.”
“O dear, then” cried Maria to her partner, “with your leave, I’ll sit down till the next.”
“So will I too, then,” cried I, “for I am sure I can hardly stand.”
“But you must speak to your partner first,” answered she; for he had turned aside to talk with some gentlemen. However, I had not sufficient courage to address him; and so away we all three tript, and seated ourselves at another end of the room.
But, unfortunately for me, Miss Mirvan soon after suffered herself to be prevailed upon to attempt the dance; and just as she rose to go, she cried, “My dear, yonder is your partner, Lord Orville walking about the room in search of you.”
“Don’t leave me then, dear girl!” cried I; but she was obliged to go. And now I was more uneasy than ever; I would have given the world to have seen Mrs. Mirvan, and begged of her to make my apologies; for what, thought I, can I possibly say to him in excuse for running away? He must either conclude me a fool, or half mad; for anyone brought up in the great world, and accustomed to its ways, can have no idea of such sort of fears as mine.
My confusion increased when I observed that he was everywhere seeking me, with apparent perplexity and surprise; but when, at last, I saw him move towards the place where I sat, I was ready to sink with shame and distress. I found it absolutely impossible to keep my seat, because I could not think of a word to say for myself; and so I rose, and walked hastily towards the cardroom, resolving to stay with Mrs. Mirvan the rest of the evening, and not to dance at all. But before I could find her, Lord Orville saw and approached me.
He begged to know if I was not well? You may easily imagine how much I was embarrassed. I made no answer; but hung my head like a fool, and looked on my fan.
He then, with an air the most respectfully serious, asked if he had been so unhappy as to offend me?
“No, indeed!” cried I; and, in hopes of changing the discourse, and preventing his further enquiries, I desired to know if he had seen the young lady who had been conversing with me?

===Chinese===

他在各方面都这样高出我一大截，把我弄得全然乱了方寸；又有一位太太走过我们身边时说："这是我见过的最难的一支舞。"您可以想见，我的胆气也没提起来多少。
"哦天，那可不行，"玛丽亚朝她的舞伴嚷道，"恕我失陪，下一场再跳。"
"那我也不跳了，"我也嚷道，"我简直站都站不住了。"
"可你得先同你的舞伴说一声呀。"她答道——他正侧过身去同几位先生说话。可我没有那份勇气去开口；于是我们三个踮着脚溜了开去，在屋子另一头坐了下来。
不料于我不幸的是，米尔文小姐不多久就被劝动去跳了；她起身时嚷道："亲爱的，你的舞伴在那边——奥维尔勋爵（Lord Orville）正满屋子找你呢。"
"那别撇下我，好姑娘！"我叫道；可她不得不去。这下我更不自在了；我肯拿全世界换一个见到米尔文太太的机会，求她替我告罪；因为，我想，我半路跑掉，还能有什么话替自己分辩？他不是把我当傻子，就是当半疯：在大家世界里长大、过惯了那套规矩的人，断然想不出我这种恐惧。
我看见他分明带着困惑和惊讶满场找我，愈发心乱；待到终于望见他朝我坐的地方走来，我羞得、窘得几乎要沉到地里去。我发现自己绝对坐不住了，因为替自己想不出一个字；于是站起身，急急朝牌局那间屋走，打定主意这一晚就陪着米尔文太太，再不跳了。可还没寻到她，奥维尔勋爵看见了我，迎了上来。
他请问我是不是不舒服？您想得出我多尴尬。我没有作声；只是像个傻子似的垂着头，盯着手里的扇子。
他又用一种极其恭谨、郑重的神气问：可是他不幸冒犯了我？
"没有，真的没有！"我叫道；一心想岔开话头、拦住他再问，我便反问：他可看见方才同我说话的那位小姐了么？

===Original===

No;﻿—but would I honour him with any commands to her?
“O, by no means!”
Was there any other person with whom I wished to speak?
I said *no*, before I knew I had answered at all.
Should he have the pleasure of bringing me any refreshment?
I bowed, almost involuntarily. And away he flew.
I was quite ashamed of being so troublesome, and so much *above* myself as these seeming airs made me appear; but indeed I was too much confused to think or act with any consistency.
If he had not been as swift as lightning, I don’t know whether I should not have stolen away again; but he returned in a moment. When I had drank a glass of lemonade, he hoped, he said, that I would again honour him with my hand, as a new dance was just begun. I had not the presence of mind to say a single word, and so I let him once more lead me to the place I had left.
Shocked to find how silly, how childish a part I had acted, my former fears of dancing before such a company, and with such a partner, returned more forcibly than ever. I suppose he perceived my uneasiness; for he entreated me to sit down again if dancing was disagreeable to me. But I was quite satisfied with the folly I had already shown; and therefore declined his offer, though I was really scarce able to stand.
Under such conscious disadvantages, you may easily imagine my dear Sir, how ill I acquitted myself. But, though I both expected and deserved to find him very much mortified and displeased at his ill fortune in the choice he had made; yet, to my very great relief, he appeared to be even contented, and very much assisted and encouraged me. These people in high life have too much presence of mind, I believe, to *seem* disconcerted, or out of humour, however they may feel: for had I been the person of the most consequence in the room, I could not have met with more attention and respect.
When the dance was over, seeing me still very much flurried, he led me to a seat, saying that he would not suffer me to fatigue myself from politeness.
And then, if my capacity, or even, if my spirits had been better, in how animated a conversation I might have been engaged! it was then I saw that the rank of Lord Orville was his least recommendation, his understanding and his manners being far more distinguished.

===Chinese===

没有；——我可否赏光，有什么话要捎给她？
"哦，万万不敢！"
那还有没有别的什么人，我想同他说话？
我答了声*没有*——答完才知道自己开了口。
他可否有幸，为我取一点提神的东西来？
我几乎不由自主地屈膝谢了。他飞身去了。
我羞极了——这样麻烦人家，而且这些看似的拿乔，显得我多么*不知天高地厚*；可我实在乱得分寸全无，想不成、也做不成任何一致的事。
若不是他快得像闪电，我说不准会不会又溜走；可他转眼就回来了。我喝过一杯柠檬水，他说，但愿我再赏他一臂之劳，一支新舞刚刚开始。我一瞬的机灵也没有，一句话也说不出，便由他又把我领回了方才离开的地方。
一想到自己方才扮演的角色多么痴、多么孩子气，先前那份在人前、而且是这样的舞伴面前跳舞的恐惧，比任何时候都凶地卷土重来。他大概看出了我的不安；恳求我说，若跳舞不适，就请再坐下。可我已经出够了丑，满足够了；于是谢绝了他的好意——虽然我实在几乎站不住。
背着这样自觉的劣势，亲爱的先生，您想得出我发挥得多糟。虽然我既料到、也认定他会为自己挑人不慎大失所望、大为扫兴；可叫我如释重负的是，他竟像还满意，处处扶助我、鼓励我。我相信，上流社会的人那份从容，多到无论如何心里怎样，也*显得*不乱、不恼：即使我是全场头一号的要人，受的殷勤与恭敬也不过如此了。
舞罢，见我还慌得很，他领我到座位上，说恕他不允许我出于客气而强撑着累坏自己。
那时，倘若我的脑力——哪怕只是兴致——好一些，我们本可以谈得多么生动！正是在那时我看出：奥维尔勋爵的爵位，是他最不足道的长处；他的见识与教养，远比爵位出众。

===Original===

His remarks upon the company in general were so apt, so just, so lively, I am almost surprised myself that they did not reanimate me; but, indeed, I was too well convinced of the ridiculous part I had myself played before so nice an observer, to be able to enjoy his pleasantry: so self-compassion gave me feeling for others. Yet I had not the courage to attempt either to defend them or to rally in my turn; but listened to him in silent embarrassment.
When he found this, he changed the subject, and talked of public places, and public performers; but he soon discovered that I was totally ignorant of them.
He then, very ingeniously, turned the discourse to the amusements and occupations of the country.
It now struck me that he was resolved to try whether or not I was capable of talking upon *any* subject. This put so great a restraint upon my thoughts, that I was unable to go further than a monosyllable, and not ever so far, when I could possibly avoid it.
We were sitting in this manner, he conversing with all gaiety, I looking down with all foolishness, when that fop who had first asked me to dance, with a most ridiculous solemnity approached, and, after a profound bow or two, said, “I humbly beg pardon, Madam﻿—and of you too, my Lord﻿—for breaking in upon such agreeable conversation﻿—which must, doubtless, be more delectable﻿—than what I have the honour to offer﻿—but﻿—”
I interrupted him﻿—I blush for my folly﻿—with laughing; yet I could not help it; for, added to the man’s stately foppishness, (and he actually took snuff between every three words) when I looked around at Lord Orville, I saw such extreme surprise in his face﻿—the cause of which appeared so absurd, that I could not for my life preserve my gravity.
I had not laughed before from the time I had left Miss Mirvan, and I had much better have cried then; Lord Orville actually stared at me; the beau, I know not his name, looked quite enraged. “Refrain﻿—Madam,” said he, with an important air, “a few moments refrain!﻿—I have but a sentence to trouble you with.﻿—May I know to what accident I must attribute not having the honour of your hand?”
“Accident, Sir!” repeated I, much astonished.
“Yes, accident, Madam;﻿—for surely﻿—I must take the liberty to observe﻿—pardon me, Madam﻿—it ought to be no common one﻿—that should tempt a lady﻿—so young a one too﻿—to be guilty of ill-manners.”

===Chinese===

他对满场宾客的那些评点，那样贴切、那样中肯、那样活泛，连我自己都吃惊，竟没能叫我重新活过来；因为我太明白，在这样一位精细的旁观者眼前，我自家那出戏演得多么可笑了，实在领受不动他的妙语：于是自怜给了我体谅旁人的心。可我又没勇气替谁分辩，也没胆子反过来打趣，只有默默地窘着听。
他见了，便换了题目，谈起公共场所和名角儿；可他很快发现，我于此道一无所知。
他便又极乖觉地把话头引到乡下的乐子和活计上。
我忽然醒悟：他这是铁了心要试试，看我究竟*配不配*谈任何一个题目。这个念头把我的思想捆得那样紧，以至于我只答得出单字——而且但凡躲得开，连单字也不答。
我们正这样坐着——他谈笑风生，我垂头尽出傻相——先前请我跳舞的那个浮华子，一脸顶可笑的庄严，踱了过来，深深一两躬之后说："小人冒昧告罪，夫人——也向您告罪，勋爵大人——打断了这样愉快的谈话——那必定——比小人斗胆要说的——可心得多——不过——"
我打断了他——我为自己的失态脸红——我笑了出来；可我实在忍不住：这个人的架子本就浮华得滑稽（他真的每说三个字就停下来嗅一次鼻烟），待我抬眼看奥维尔勋爵，又见他脸上那样极致的惊愕——而那缘故又那样荒唐，我拼了命也板不住脸。
自撇下米尔文小姐起，这是我头一回笑，而那时我倒不如哭；奥维尔勋爵直瞪着我；那位纨袴子——我不知道他姓甚名谁——一脸怒气。"收敛些，夫人，"他拿腔作势地说，"稍敛片刻！——小人只讨您一句话。——敢问夫人，小人错失执您一臂之荣，当归咎于何等变故呀？"
"变故，先生！"我惊得直重复。
"正是变故，夫人；——因为恕小人放肆直言——夫人恕罪——那必定不是一桩寻常变故——才引得一位淑女——还是这样年轻的一位——失礼于人。"

===Original===

A confused idea now for the first time entered my head, of something I had heard of the rules of an assembly; but I was never at one before﻿—I have only danced at school﻿—and so giddy and heedless I was, that I had not once considered the impropriety of refusing one partner, and afterwards accepting another. I was thunderstruck at the recollection: but, while these thoughts were rushing into my head, Lord Orville with some warmth, said, “This Lady, Sir, is incapable of meriting such an accusation!”
The creature﻿—for I am very angry with him﻿—made a low bow and with a grin the most malicious I ever saw, “My Lord,” said he, “far be it from me to *accuse* the lady, for having the discernment to distinguish and prefer﻿—the superior attractions of your Lordship.”
Again he bowed and walked off.
Was ever anything so provoking? I was ready to die with shame. “What a coxcomb!” exclaimed Lord Orville: while I, without knowing what I did, rose hastily, and moving off, “I can’t imagine,” cried I, “where Mrs. Mirvan has hid herself!”
“Give me leave to see,” answered he. I bowed and sat down again, not daring to meet his eyes; for what must he think of me, between my blunder, and the supposed preference?
He returned in a moment, and told me that Mrs. Mirvan was at cards, but would be glad to see me; and I went immediately. There was but one chair vacant; so, to my great relief, Lord Orville presently left us. I then told Mrs. Mirvan my disasters; and she good-naturedly blamed herself for not having better instructed me; but said, she had taken it for granted that I must know such common customs. However, the man may, I think, be satisfied with his pretty speech and carry his resentment no farther.
In a short time Lord Orville returned. I consented, with the best grace I could, to go down another dance, for I had had time to recollect myself; and therefore resolved to use some exertion, and, if possible, to appear less a fool than I had hitherto done; for it occurred to me, that, insignificant as I was, compared to a man of his rank and figure; yet, since he had been so unfortunate as to make choice of me for a partner, why I should endeavour to make the best of it.
The dance, however, was short, and he spoke very little; so I had no opportunity of putting my resolution in practice.

===Chinese===

此刻，一个懵懂的念头头一回钻进我脑子：我似乎听说过，舞会自有舞会的规矩；可我从没到过舞会——我只在学校里跳过——我又那样晕头转向、心不在焉，竟压根没想过：辞了一位舞伴、随后又应另一位，是何等失当。想到这里，我如遭雷击；可就在这些念头涌上来时，奥维尔勋爵带着几分火气开了口："先生，这位女士决当不起这样的指控！"
那个东西——我正在气他——深深一躬，咧出一个我生平仅见的最恶毒的笑："勋爵大人，"他说，"小人万不敢*指控*夫人明察秋毫、善于甄别——竟垂青了大人您更胜一筹的魅力。"
他又是一躬，扬长而去。
世上还有比这更气人的么？我羞得要死。"好一个自负的蠢货！"奥维尔勋爵脱口喊道；而我不假思索地霍然起身，躲了开去："真想不通，"我叫道，"米尔文太太躲到哪儿去了！"
"容我去看看。"他答道。我屈膝谢了，重新坐下，不敢看他的眼睛；夹在我的失态和那份"垂青"之间，他该怎么想我！
他片刻便回，告诉我米尔文太太在牌桌上，愿意见我；我立刻过去了。那里恰只空着一把椅子，所以奥维尔勋爵随即离开了我们，真叫我如释重负。我把我的灾祸一一讲给米尔文太太听；她好心肠地怪自己没先教教我；又说，她原以为这样的寻常规矩，我必定是懂的。不过依我看，那位先生有了他那漂亮话，也该满意，火气不必再发了。
不多时，奥维尔勋爵又来了。我竭力拿出最好的风度，答应再跳一支——这一回我有了定神的时候，便打定主意拼一拼，能少像个傻子就少像个傻子；因为我想起来了：比起他那样身份地位的人，我纵然微不足道，可他既不幸挑了我作舞伴，我就该尽力把这差事办得像样些。
然而那支舞很短，他话说得也很少；我的决心没得机会用上。

===Original===

He was satisfied, I suppose, with his former successless efforts to draw me out or, rather, I fancied he had been enquiring *who I was*. This again disconcerted me; and the spirits I had determined to exert, again failed me. Tired, ashamed, and mortified, I begged to sit down till we returned home, which I did soon after. Lord Orville did me the honour to hand me to the coach, talking all the way of the honour *I* had done *him*! O these fashionable people!
Well, my dear Sir, was it not a strange evening? I could not help being thus particular, because, to me, everything is so new. But it is now time to conclude. I am, with all love and duty, your
Evelina.

===Chinese===

他先前引我开口，回回无功，我猜他是灰了心——或者不如说，我疑心他一直在打听*我是谁*。这又叫我慌了；我打定要抖擞的那点精神，又塌了下去。我又累、又羞、又臊，只求坐着等回家——不久我们也就回了。奥维尔勋爵赏光，一路送我上马车，满口说的全是*我*赏给*他*的脸面！哦，这些时髦人儿！
怎么样，亲爱的先生，这晚上奇不奇怪？我忍不住写得这样细，因为于我，样样都这样新鲜。可是该收笔了。我怀着全部的爱与孝敬，是您的
伊芙琳娜。

## Letter / 书信
===Original===

XII Evelina in Continuation
Tuesday, April 5.
There is to be no end to the troubles of last night. I have this moment, between persuasion and laughter, gathered from Maria the most curious dialogue that ever I heard. You will at first be startled at my vanity; but, my dear Sir, have patience!
It must have passed while I was sitting with Mrs. Mirvan, in the cardroom. Maria was taking some refreshment, and saw Lord Orville advancing for the same purpose himself; but he did not know her, though she immediately recollected him. Presently after, a very gay-looking man, stepping hastily up to him cried, “Why, my Lord, what have you done with your lovely partner?”
